raw_segments.text: It was impossible at the foundation of the States, and it would still be difficult to
establish a central administration in America.
The inhabitants are dispersed over too great a space and separated by too many natural
obstacles for one man to undertake to direct the details of their existence.
America is therefore preeminently the country of provincial and municipal government.
To this cause, which was plainly felt by all the Europeans of the New World, the Anglo-Americans
added several others peculiar to themselves.
